The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: the Pustet Ratisbon 1862 layer reads 'beaJ t6rum Petn,' where the 1962 prints 'beatorum Petri'; recogniser damage, letterforms inferred not read; conclusion length only: the Pustet Ratisbon 1862 stops at the short cue; the words that follow it in the witness ('Festo Ss. Martyrum Tryphonis et. Sociorum,') are the book's own rubric, not part of the prayer, and the 1962 continues 'unitate.'; pointing was NOT collated: this comparison is word-level, because the witness reaches me as an optical text layer whose commas, colons and full stops are unreliable. propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Deus, qui nos annua beatorum Martyrum tuorum Marcellini, Petri atque Erasmi
solemnitate laetificas: praesta, quaesumus; ut, quorum gaudemus meritis,
accendamur exemplis. Per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, Filium tuum: Qui
tecum vivit et regnat in unitate.

propers.name: Secret
propers.text:
Haec hostia, quaesumus, Domine, quam sanctorum Martyrum tuorum natalicia
recensentes offerimus, et vincula nostrae pravitatis absolvat, et tuae nobis
misericordiae dona conciliet. Per Dominum.

propers.name: Postcommunion
propers.text:
Sacro munere satiati, supplices te, Domine, deprecamur: ut, quod debitae
servitutis celebramus officio, salvationis tuae sentiamus augmentum. Per
Dominum.
